top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Sellaronda Bike Day's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.

Road-specific control matters at Sellaronda Bike Day. Practice on paved Dolomite mountain pass roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 33 miles.
5,413ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Sellaronda Bike Day, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
164ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
5,413ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
33 miles on paved Dolomite mountain pass roads burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Sellaronda Bike Day. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Sellaronda Bike Day. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 5,413ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved Dolomite mountain pass roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Base fitness for Sellaronda Bike Day. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.

race_overlay.heat: June in Sella Group, Dolomites, Italy can bring heat. Complete 3–4 heat exposure sessions in the final 2 weeks before Sellaronda Bike Day. Increase sodium intake 48 hours before race day.
race_overlay.nutrition: Standard hydration and fueling. One bottle per hour minimum. Gel or bar every 45 minutes at race intensity.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at Sellaronda Bike Day. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Sellaronda Bike Day requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on paved dolomite mountain pass roads to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, Road Specific, and VO2max to prepare you for 33 miles of paved dolomite mountain pass roads in Sella Group, Dolomites, Italy.
